passages.context: Canon 1268 §§1–4 limits habitual reservation to one altar in a church, directs reservation to the church's preeminent and noblest place and therefore ordinarily the high altar, states the cathedral, collegiate, and conventual choral-function exception favoring another chapel or altar, and requires the reservation altar to be ornamented above the others. It controls reservation topology and relative status, not altar, tabernacle, ornament, or architectural morphology.

alternate_titles: Codex Iuris Canonici Pii X Pontificis Maximi iussu digestus Benedicti Papae XV auctoritate promulgatus
work.author: Catholic Church; promulgated by Benedict XV
work.description: The first codification of Latin-church canon law, digested by order of Pius X and promulgated by Benedict XV by the apostolic constitution Providentissima Mater Ecclesia of 27 May 1917, in force from 19 May 1918 until it was replaced by the 1983 Code. Canon 2335 attached an ipso facto excommunication simply reserved to the Apostolic See to those enrolling in the Masonic sect or other associations of the same kind machinating against the Church or legitimate civil authorities.
work.title: Codex Iuris Canonici (1917)
